prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” digital marketing agency in St. Louis — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, timeline and industry. I can help you find the best fit. To get started, answer one question: what are you trying to accomplish (examples: increase e‑commerce sales, generate B2B leads, improve local SEO, run paid ads, rebrand)?

Meanwhile, here are quick, practical next steps and how I’ll evaluate candidates for you:

What matters when picking an agency
- Primary goals and KPIs (sales, leads, traffic, brand awareness)  
- Services needed (SEO, PPC, social media, content, email, web design, analytics)  
- Budget range and contract length  
- Industry experience / case studies in your niche  
- Team size and whether you prefer local in‑person work or remote  
- Reporting cadence and transparency (access to data, dashboards)  

Where to find and check agencies
- Clutch.co, UpCity, G2, Google My Business for reviews and client testimonials  
- Agency case studies and metrics (not just creative work — look for results)  
- LinkedIn for client/employee feedback and recent hires  
- Ask for references and talk to a past client in your industry  

Questions to ask each agency
- What KPIs do you recommend for my goal and why?  
- Can you show 1–2 case studies with measurable results?  
- Who will be my day‑to‑day contact and what does the team look like?  
- What tools and reporting will I get? How often?  
- What is your pricing model (retainer, project, performance)?  
- What does success look like at 3, 6, 12 months?  

Red flags
- Vague promises like “we’ll get you to #1 on Google” without strategy  
- No clear KPIs or reporting process  
- Poor communication during the proposal stage  
- No client references or only cherry‑picked, unverified results  

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 4–6 St. Louis agencies matched to your goals and budget (I’ll include strengths, sample clients, and questions to ask each), or  
- Draft an RFP you can use to vet agencies.

Tell me your primary goal, budget (rough), and whether you prefer local agencies — I’ll build a tailored shortlist.
